# Reporting Results: Tables, Figures, and Honest Prose

## The Rule of Three Numbers

Every quantitative claim should include: the estimate, its uncertainty (CI or SE), and the sample size.

> *"New scheduler reduced median latency from 12.4 ms to 10.8 ms (delta = -1.6 ms; bootstrap 95% CI: -2.1, -1.0; n = 30 runs x 10 benchmarks; Wilcoxon paired p < .001; Cliff's delta = 0.62)."*

## Figures

- One claim per figure.
- Axes labeled with units.
- Log scale when data span orders of magnitude.
- Color-blind safe palettes (`viridis`).
- No 3D bar charts.

## Tables

Minimal lines, right-aligned numbers, consistent significant digits. Three significant figures is almost always enough.

## Honest Prose

- Distinguish "significant" (statistical) from "important" (practical).
- Report negative and null results.
- Acknowledge threats to validity in a dedicated section.
